text:
maya: Thanks for the AH today — quick follow-ups on the runway and procurement items mentioned. A few specific Qs: 1) who should we ping for procurement exceptions (e.g., vendor integrations)? 2) P-card vs PO guidance for infra spending? 3) When do reserved capacity commits need exec sign-off?

lucas: +1 on reserved capacity. Our infra team is considering a 6mo commit for Dedicated GPUs — who signs and what's the threshold?

maria (CFO): Great questions — short answers: exceptions -> finance-ops (cc @dylan) for initial triage; P-card ok for <= $5k one-off infra purchases; PO required for > $5k or multi-month commits. Exec sign-off for reserved commits >= $50k ARR equivalent.

maya: thanks! is that $50k annualized or total contract value?

maria (CFO): annualized. Example: a 12-mo Dedicated commit that costs $6k/mo -> $72k annualized -> needs exec sign-off.

dylan (Finance Ops): For exceptions we run a quick form (link below) then Finance Ops routes to security/legal if needed. Please include: business case, data residency, expected term, and owner. Ticket template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-234 (use this to track).

tanya: For P-card, any special vendor onboarding steps? vendors with infra access need SSO + ATO checklist, right?

maria (CFO): correct. P-card purchases that touch infra still require onboarding. If vendor will run workloads in our infra or has access to customer data, route through vendor-onboarding and security.

ashley: re: reserved capacity approvals — will product discounting / committed rates be negotiated by sales or procurement?

dylan (Finance Ops): Procurement handles commercial terms for Dedicated commits; Sales can negotiate non-standard discounts but must loop in Procurement + Finance Ops for approvals. Use this approval flow snippet for clarity:
```
Requester -> Manager (budget check) -> Finance Ops (policy) -> Procurement (terms) -> CFO/Exec if >= $50k annualized
```

lucas: helpful — any SLA or rollback guidance if we commit and need to scale down?

maria (CFO): We try to keep flexibility in terms. Standard Dedicated contracts include a 30-day notice for scaling changes; true exceptions are handled case-by-case during procurement. If you expect variability, flag it early in the form.

maya: Action items for infra/product teams: 1) fill FIN-234 template for any upcoming commits; 2) note expected utilization curve; 3) cc @dylan and @maria.

procure-bot: Created FIN-234-1: "6mo Dedicated commit inquiry from infra" and assigned to dylan.

sam (CEO): Appreciate the clarifications. High level: we want to balance runway and velocity — if a committed deal materially reduces unit cost and has a clear ROI, we will support it. But keep Finance in the loop early. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks all — I'll share this summary with the team and attach the form. If anyone needs me to shepherd a request, ping me. :pray:
